newsitem.title: UK: UK shares close higher but further losses expected.
newsitem.headline: UK shares close higher but further losses expected.

text.p: UK shares finished higher on Monday, the first day of the new British tax year, as FTSE 100 shadowed a firmer Wall Street.
But continued worries about possible near-term U.S. and UK rate hikes were expected to put a cap on any FTSE advance, dealers and strategists said.

"We've had a predictable bounce today but not a convincing bounce," one senior dealer said. "People are afraid that if U.S. rates keep going up the Dow (Industrials Average) will head lower, dragging the FTSE with it."
The FTSE 100 closed 35.1 points up at 4,271.7.
The Dow Industrials Average, which has slumped around eight percent since the middle of last month, was up about 45 points by the London close.
The FTSE 100 share index has risen around 57 points or 1.3 percent over the past two trading days, after dropping nearly 100 points the preceding three sessions.
"The market was oversold and we've seen a technical rally," said Kirit Shah, strategist at Sanwa International.
"The FTSE is still in a downtrend. But for the next couple of days we could see a technical bounce."
